claims.text: Conventional metallic alloys processed using traditional methods typically exhibit high strength but reduced ductility.
The reduced ductility of traditionally processed high-strength alloys is caused by established microstructural characteristics.
Machine-learning models trained on multiscale experimental and simulation data can identify advantageous processing windows.
Machine-learning models can optimize alloy compositions to overcome the strength–ductility trade-off.
The proposed approach can be applied under standard processing environments without specialized high-pressure or temperature conditions.
ML-guided processing and composition optimization will produce microstructures with balanced feature distributions.
Refined grain size and controlled precipitate distributions can enable simultaneous improvements in strength and ductility.
Analysis of large materials datasets allows an ML model to identify non-intuitive combinations of processing parameters and compositions.
The combinations identified by ML lead to microstructures that mitigate the strength–ductility constraint.
Strengthening mechanisms such as grain refinement or precipitation hardening typically cause embrittlement.
ML-guided optimization can decouple strength and ductility in conventional alloys.
ML-optimized materials will exhibit significant simultaneous improvements in yield or ultimate strength and ductility relative to conventionally processed counterparts.
The benefits of the approach are limited to alloys and processing conditions that are well represented in the training dataset.
The approach may not generalize to novel alloy systems outside the training-data regime.
The magnitude of mechanical-property improvements depends on the quality and breadth of the training datasets.
